subject: Renewal + capacity increase — MSA/redline coordination
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@northforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2024 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal & capacity bump (Northforge)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the quick chat yesterday. Northforge is ready to move forward with renewal but we need to: 1) extend the term to 24 months, 2) add 250k additional inference units spread across Q3–Q4, and 3) lock pricing at the proposed uplift rate.

Attached is a short forecast and a marked MSA that our procurement team prefers (Northforge_MSA_redline_from-customer.docx). Key asks from our side:
- Term: 24 months (effective 2024-06-01)
- Capacity: +250k inference units (order form to reflect tiered ramp)
- Invoicing: annual in advance, but procurement will process PO after countersignature

Can you confirm Redwood’s approach to the term wording and whether the data retention / audit language in section 7 can be aligned with our edits? Procurement contact: procurement@northforge.com (cc'd).

Best,
Ari Patel
Head of Platform
Northforge, Inc.

Attachment: Northforge_Renewal_Request_20240514.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: Northforge_MSA_redline_from-customer.docx (tracked changes)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari@northforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2024 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & capacity bump (Northforge)

Ari — thanks for the clear summary and the file. We're excited to continue and appreciate the forecast. Quick plan from our side:

1) I'll loop in Legal (Ben) and AM (Laura) to review the MSA edits and the order form changes.
2) Ben — can you review the customer's redline (attached) and flag any non-starters? Laura will confirm the ramp schedule in the order form and check pricing math.
3) Ari / procurement — can you confirm the preferred sign date (you mentioned effective 2024-06-01) and whether there are any PO naming/line-item constraints we should be aware of?

We have internal guardrails around data-retention and SLA credits — Ben, please prioritize section 7 (data retention) and the SLA credit calculation so we can get a quick counter.

I'll coordinate a short 30-minute call if that helps move this faster; suggest Thu 5/16 morning PT if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Northforge_MSA_redline_from-customer.docx (forwarded)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ari Patel <ari@northforge.com>, procurement@northforge.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal & capacity bump (Northforge)

Hannah / Ari — reviewing the customer's redline now. Summary of our position and next steps below (high level):

- Term extension to 24 months: acceptable from a commercial perspective. We will need a clarification on automatic renewal language — propose to keep renewal opt-in (explicit consent) rather than auto-renew to match our standard playbook.
- Capacity uplift and order form: Laura, please confirm the tiered ramp language and whether the +250k can be split as quarterly increments.
- Data retention / audit language (section 7): customer's edit attempts to broaden access for third-party audits. We cannot accept those changes as written. Proposed revision: allow audit rights limited to security and SOC-related scoped evidence only, with minimum 30 days' notice and mutually-agreed scope.
- SLA credits and cap: we can agree to the uplift but propose a soft cap on credits at 100% of one month’s average monthly spend during the prior 3 months.

Attached are our annotated artifacts: Redwood_MSA_marked_v2.docx (track changes + comments) and a clean PDF showing the differential on the OrderForm (OrderForm_Northforge_2024-05.pdf).

If Ari is comfortable with limited audit scope and the SLA cap language, we can prepare a final countersigned MSA and push a DocuSign envelope. I can fast-track the legal sign-off if procurement accepts the two items above.

Proposed next step: Hannah to confirm ramp schedule and Ari to confirm acceptance of audit scope + SLA cap. If yes, I'll publish the DocuSign envelope and share the link.

Ben Carter
Senior Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_MSA_marked_v2.docx (track changes + comments)
Attachment: OrderForm_Northforge_2024-05.pdf (clean diff)
From: Ari Patel <ari@northforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northforge.com, Maya Singh <m.singh@northforge.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2024 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & capacity bump (Northforge)

Ben / Hannah — thanks for the quick review and the proposed counter. We had a brief run by procurement and security:

- Audit scope: we can accept the limited audit language you proposed (security/SOC only, 30 days notice, mutually agreed scope).
- SLA credit cap: acceptable to Northforge as long as the calculation method is clearly documented on the order form (monthly average of prior 3 months).
- Term: 24 months effective 2024-06-01 — agreed.

Procurement notes: once the DocuSign envelope is complete we'll route internally and should be able to issue a PO within 5 business days. Please include the final invoice line (annual in advance) and a billing contact on the order form for our AP team (m.singh@northforge.com).

Can we get the DocuSign envelope this morning so procurement can begin routing?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this wrapped.

Best,
Ari Patel
Head of Platform, Northforge
